title: Fresh Mozzarella and Peach Salad
subtitle: Buffalo mozzarella with ripe summer peaches, basil and olive oil
excerpt: Torn buffalo mozzarella with ripe peach slices, rocket, fresh basil and a drizzle of good olive oil and balsamic glaze. A five-minute summer lunch that needs perfect ingredients.
sourceNotes: The combination of fresh mozzarella with summer fruit is a modern Italian variation on the caprese theme, pairing the creamy cheese with sweet seasonal fruit rather than tomatoes. Buffalo mozzarella (mozzarella di bufala) from Campania, produced from the milk of water buffalo, is richer and creamier than the cow's milk version and became widely available in British food retailers from the 1990s onward.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble within 20 minutes of serving. Remove the mozzarella from the fridge 30 minutes before serving.

content.text: Fresh mozzarella and peach is a salad that asks nothing of the cook beyond choosing the right ingredients. The mozzarella must be fresh buffalo mozzarella from a bag of whey, not the firm block in brine; the peaches must be ripe enough to smell sweet and give when pressed. Take the cheese out of the fridge 30 minutes before serving: cold mozzarella is flavourless and rubbery.

items.prepNote: drained and torn into rough pieces
ripe, halved, stoned and sliced into wedges

content.text: Arrange the rocket on a large plate or platter. Lay the peach wedges and {{mozzarella-di-bufala}} of torn mozzarella over the rocket, alternating them. Scatter the basil leaves over the top. Drizzle generously with {{olive-oil}} of extra-virgin olive oil. Add a drizzle of balsamic glaze if using. Sprinkle with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Used cold from the fridge, or is a long-life firm block rather than fresh.
items.fix: Remove from the fridge 30 minutes before serving. Use fresh buffalo mozzarella in whey (Mozzarella di Bufala Campana DOP if available). Cold mozzarella has almost no flavour.

Only make this salad in summer. Peaches ripen best at room temperature; refrigerating them stops ripening and destroys texture. Nectarines are a reliable substitute when peaches are hard to find ripe.

content.text: Fresh mozzarella with summer fruit extends the caprese idea into stone fruit. The combination became popular in British restaurant cooking in the 2000s and moved into home cooking as buffalo mozzarella became more widely available. The menu of things to do is short: choose good fruit, choose good cheese, add oil and basil.
